inspection_summary: Inspected all 403 normalized lines. The source gives a formal, explicitly conditional spectral construction: a difference-operator similarity transform produces Hurwitz-zeta eigenfunctions, and a boundary value selects Riemann-zeta zeros. Its reusable depth also includes asymptotic exclusion of trivial-zero states, a modified-PT and pseudo-Hermitian heuristic, a biorthogonal metric and distributional orthogonality test, exceptional-point consequences for off-critical zeros, and an epsilon-family approaching a Berry-Keating representative. The paper repeatedly states that the domain, completeness, bounded-inverse, normalizability, and self-adjointness issues remain unresolved, so none of the construction is treated here as a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. Two-column extraction leaves several displayed formulas visually interleaved; accepted claims are limited to those recoverable from adjacent prose, with original-PDF verification requested where exact formulas matter.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Identifies the paper and summarizes the proposed Hamiltonian, conditional boundary-spectrum correspondence, classical limit, modified-PT claim, metric heuristic, and unresolved self-adjointness requirement.

sections_inspected.label: Zeta background and spectral proposal
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces zeta representations and the RH/Hilbert-Polya motivation, then states the Hamiltonian and the paper's five principal conditional findings.

sections_inspected.label: Preliminaries: difference operator and restricted inverse
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Represents the Hamiltonian as a similarity transform of the dilation Hamiltonian, identifies the finite-difference kernel obstruction, and defines an inverse only with decay-at-infinity and Borel-summation qualifications.

sections_inspected.label: Eigenfunctions, zeros, and asymptotic domain discrimination
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives Hurwitz-zeta eigenfunctions, turns the origin boundary condition into the zeta-zero condition, contrasts trivial and nontrivial asymptotics, and marks the subsequent reality argument as heuristic.

sections_inspected.label: Modified PT, pseudo-Hermiticity, Berry-Keating representatives, and biorthogonal setup
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops the conditional symmetry route, related Hermitian representatives and quantization condition, adjoint eigenstates, and the metric-defined inner product.

sections_inspected.label: Biorthogonality, boundary terms, degeneracies, regularization, and open domain problem
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses a distributional pairing to distinguish nontrivial from trivial states, relates the origin boundary condition to momentum symmetry, states exceptional-point consequences, notes infinite norms and a cutoff regularization, and isolates domain/completeness as open.

sections_inspected.label: References and epsilon-family note
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Contains bibliography plus a substantive note deforming the difference operator through an epsilon-family whose limiting representative has power-law eigenstates.

accepted_units.title: Difference-conjugated Hamiltonian as a conditional zero spectrum
accepted_units.why_material: The source states its central construction and separates several consequences: the origin boundary condition maps spectral parameters to nontrivial zeta zeros, the commuting limit is 2xp, modified PT symmetry supplies a possible reality route, a new inner product is proposed, and off-critical zeros would produce degeneracy.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the authors' overview; the supporting constructions and their qualifications occur later. It is a conditional program, not an established self-adjoint realization or an RH proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (1), fractions, operator ordering, and the critical-line notation are formula-bearing and should be checked against the retained PDF before exact symbolic reuse; the prose-level claims are legible.

accepted_units.title: Finite difference, its kernel, and a decay-qualified inverse
accepted_units.why_material: Writing the proposed Hamiltonian as a similarity transform through Delta exposes the key structural issue: Delta is a unit shift difference, annihilates unit-periodic functions, and therefore has no inverse on all smooth functions. The authors restrict attention to functions vanishing at infinity and give a Bernoulli/Borel prescription whose right-inverse property is tied to that boundary choice.
accepted_units.context_note: The inverse is formal for some functions and is explicitly described as Borel summable; no unrestricted operator inverse or complete domain is established.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The two-column extraction interleaves equations (2)-(4), contour integrals, and prose. Exact coefficients, contour orientation, and inverse-operator placement require original-PDF verification, while the kernel and boundary-at-infinity mechanism is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Hurwitz-zeta eigenfunctions and boundary selection of zeta zeros
accepted_units.why_material: The Borel-summed inverse applied to a power is recognized as a Hurwitz-zeta representation. The resulting eigenfunction is minus the Hurwitz zeta, and imposing its value at the origin to vanish makes the spectral parameter a zero of the Riemann zeta function.
accepted_units.context_note: The additive unit-periodic ambiguity is removed by the eigenvalue equation according to the source. The single origin condition is motivated by the similarity to a first-order differential operator and later by momentum symmetry.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed contour and eigenvalue formulas are extraction-risky; verify them in the PDF for exact normalization and signs. The identification, periodic-ambiguity statement, and boundary-to-zero implication are recoverable from the prose.

accepted_units.title: Asymptotics separate trivial-zero states from the proposed domain
accepted_units.why_material: The source contrasts polynomially growing Bernoulli-polynomial states at trivial zeros with sublinear nontrivial-zero states, and correspondingly distinguishes whether Delta applied to the state vanishes at infinity. Together with the later orthogonality behavior, this is used to exclude trivial-zero states from the Hamiltonian domain while retaining a discrete spectrum indexed by nontrivial zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The claimed RH equivalence is only that reality of these formally obtained eigenvalues matches real part one-half for the selected zeros; it does not establish that the operator realization is self-adjoint.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Page-boundary and two-column extraction split several asymptotic formulas. Check the Bernoulli-polynomial normalization, powers, and eigenvalue-to-zero formula against the PDF; the growth comparison and domain conclusion are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Reality of the spectrum is left to a heuristic symmetry analysis
accepted_units.why_material: The authors explicitly distinguish their complex extension of the Berry-Keating idea from the missing proof that the eigenvalues are real, and announce the limited route they pursue: modified PT symmetry, pseudo-Hermiticity, an isospectral Berry-Keating representative, and a biorthogonal inner product.
accepted_units.context_note: This span is important negative information: it prevents the ensuing formal calculations from being misread as a completed proof.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose is recoverable despite two-column interleaving; exact representative formulas mentioned in the adjacent column are treated in separate units and require formula verification.

accepted_units.title: Modified parity-time reflection gives a conditional spectral-reality route
accepted_units.why_material: After interchanging the usual roles assigned to coordinate and momentum, the source defines PT to fix x and reverse p, making iH invariant. It then uses the broken/unbroken PT eigenvalue alternatives to state that maximal breaking for iH would make the spectrum of H real, while distinguishing the behavior asserted for nontrivial and trivial zero states.
accepted_units.context_note: Broken PT symmetry by itself is not presented as sufficient for RH; the needed condition is maximal breaking in the spectral sense stated by the authors.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The transformation laws and PT action on eigenstates contain symbols vulnerable to extraction. Verify exact signs and subscripts in the PDF before symbolic reuse; the conditional logic is readable in prose.

accepted_units.title: Conditional metric and formally Hermitian representatives
accepted_units.why_material: Assuming the momentum operator is symmetric on the eventual domain, the source computes an adjoint relation with a nonnegative metric based on sin-squared of half the momentum, then discusses similarity transforms yielding a Hamiltonian with a quantum-anomaly momentum term or the Berry-Keating dilation Hamiltonian. It also records the decisive obstruction that the inverse metric is unbounded.
accepted_units.context_note: This page is physically interleaved by two-column extraction. The construction depends on the unproved domain-level symmetry of momentum, and standard bounded-metric isospectral criteria do not directly apply because the inverse is unbounded; the authors instead claim a direct calculation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: All metric, adjoint, rho, and transformed-Hamiltonian formulas should be checked against the retained PDF. Accepted content is restricted to the prose-supported conditional construction and its stated unbounded-inverse limitation.

accepted_units.title: Boundary transport to a Berry-Keating quantization condition
accepted_units.why_material: A similarity representative with Berry-Keating Hamiltonian has power-law eigenstates, and the source transports the original origin boundary condition through a sine-of-momentum relation to an explicit limiting quantization condition involving the Hurwitz zeta function.
accepted_units.context_note: This is a formal transport of the boundary condition, not a proof that a self-adjoint Berry-Keating domain with the desired spectrum exists.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The power, half-shifts, limits, and arguments in the displayed quantization condition are visually fragmented. Original-PDF verification is required before using the exact condition; only the representation-change mechanism is accepted from the extracted text.

accepted_units.title: Adjoint eigenstates define a metric pairing for the non-Hermitian eigenbasis
accepted_units.why_material: The source replaces ordinary orthogonality by eigenstates of the formal adjoint, gives their forward-difference form, and defines an associated-state map and inner product on the span of the original eigenstates. This makes the metric operator the bridge between non-Hermitian spectral data and a symmetry claim.
accepted_units.context_note: The construction is conditional on the displayed operator actually being the Hermitian adjoint on a suitable domain. The source also warns that the resulting space is not a Hilbert space because the states have infinite norm.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The adjoint formula, forward-difference state, metric, and integral pairing are formula-dependent and should be verified in the PDF; their roles and the non-Hilbert-space warning are legible in prose.

accepted_units.title: Distributional pairing distinguishes nontrivial from trivial states
accepted_units.why_material: The biorthogonal pairing is reduced to a scale-invariant power integral. Under the source's RH-conditioned conjugacy relation it is interpreted as a Dirac delta, giving off-diagonal biorthogonality, whereas the analogous integral for trivial-zero states diverges too strongly even as a tempered distribution.
accepted_units.context_note: This is distributional rather than Hilbert-space normalizability, and its RH-conditioned step cannot independently establish RH.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Equation (6), its exponent, the delta normalization, and conjugations are extraction-sensitive and require PDF verification. The contrast between distributional nontrivial-state pairing and excessive trivial-state divergence is explicit.

accepted_units.title: The origin boundary condition is reused to suppress integration-by-parts terms
accepted_units.why_material: Because the metric commutes with momentum, the source reduces momentum symmetry to vanishing boundary terms in paired original and adjoint states. The adjoint state diverges at the origin, so sufficient vanishing of the original state is needed; the already imposed condition at zero is said to suffice. Under that assumption, a formal integral rearrangement makes H symmetric in the new inner product.
accepted_units.context_note: The argument links spectral selection and operator symmetry through the same boundary condition, but it remains conditional on the domain and adjoint assumptions and does not prove self-adjointness.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The integration-by-parts expressions and operator rearrangement across lines 281-296 are heavily interleaved. Verify exact algebra in the PDF; the boundary-term logic and conditional conclusion are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Off-critical zeros are represented as exceptional-point degeneracies
accepted_units.why_material: The source claims that if RH is false, eigenstates associated with off-critical nontrivial zeros coalesce into Jordan-block structures and satisfy self-orthogonality. It then connects spectral nondegeneracy to simplicity of zeros, but explicitly makes the strongest simplicity conclusion depend on a one-to-one correspondence between eigenstate boundary conditions and the secular equation.
accepted_units.context_note: The exceptional-point and simplicity statements are consequences within the formal spectral model. The one-to-one correspondence needed for the all-roots simplicity conclusion is posed conditionally, not proved here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The key claims are readable in prose; the self-orthogonality notation and critical-line fraction should be checked against the PDF for exact transcription.

accepted_units.title: Infinite norms motivate a finite-window regularization
accepted_units.why_material: The source separates its formal Hamiltonian analysis from ordinary quantum mechanics because the states are not normalizable, then proposes a symmetric multiplicative cutoff, logarithmic state renormalization, and a limit. It reports that the transformed-position expectation has the same leading scale as prime counting.
accepted_units.context_note: This is offered as a possible physical connection, not as validation of the spectral construction or an exact prime-counting theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The cutoff interval, normalization power, transformed position, and asymptotic expectation are formula-bearing and require original-PDF verification before quantitative use; the obstruction and proposed regularization are prose-supported.

accepted_units.title: Domain and completeness remain the unresolved self-adjointness bottleneck
accepted_units.why_material: The discussion identifies the domain of H and establishment of self-adjointness as difficult open problems. The boundary-condition revisit further notes that finite-dimensional biorthogonality logic does not automatically pass to the infinite-dimensional setting: completeness of the proposed eigenstates is needed to identify the displayed operator as the Hermitian adjoint.
accepted_units.context_note: This limitation is source-specific and blocks upgrading formal symmetry or pseudo-Hermiticity to a rigorous RH implication.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The mathematical caveat is stated in prose and is not dependent on reconstructing damaged formulas.

accepted_units.title: An epsilon-family interpolates the finite difference toward a power-law representative
accepted_units.why_material: A substantive note embedded among the references replaces the unit difference by an epsilon-scaled difference, gives Hurwitz-zeta eigenstates with rescaled argument and unchanged spectral parameter, and states that the zero-epsilon limit yields a momentum-conjugated dilation Hamiltonian with a power-law eigenstate.
accepted_units.context_note: The note supplies a representation-level bridge between the nonlocal difference construction and a limiting Berry-Keating-type operator; it does not resolve the domain or self-adjointness problem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The scaled difference, proportionality, limiting operator, and eigenstate exponent are formula-dependent. Verify equation typography and operator order against the retained PDF before exact use.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: From finite difference to zeta-zero boundary spectrum
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source's core chain is representation-theoretic: conjugate a dilation operator by a decay-qualified finite difference inverse, identify the resulting power inverse with a Hurwitz-zeta eigenfunction, impose the origin value to select Riemann-zeta zeros, and use asymptotics to exclude trivial-zero states from the proposed domain.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The inverse, domain, and displayed formulas are formal or extraction-sensitive, and the chain does not establish self-adjointness or completeness.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Conditional non-Hermitian route from symmetry to spectral reality
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Modified PT symmetry, a pseudo-Hermitian metric, adjoint eigenstates, and a biorthogonal pairing are assembled to make H formally symmetric under the same boundary condition that selects zeros.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Every upgrade to a rigorous reality result depends on unresolved domain, adjoint, boundedness, completeness, and self-adjointness questions; distributional orthogonality is not normalizability.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Difference-scale deformation toward Berry-Keating form
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The source relates the nonlocal finite-difference Hamiltonian to Berry-Keating-type representatives both by similarity transport of the boundary condition and by shrinking an epsilon-scaled difference toward a momentum-conjugated dilation operator.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The exact transported quantization formula and limiting operator order require scan verification, and neither bridge supplies a self-adjoint domain.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Internal diagnostics for a failed spectral realization
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Growth, excessive distributional divergence, self-orthogonality, Jordan coalescence, infinite norm, and missing completeness function as distinct diagnostics of which proposed states or operator claims fail and why.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Some diagnostics are conditional consequences of the formal model or of RH itself and therefore cannot serve as independent evidence for RH.

within_source_saturation: All 403 lines were dispositioned. Further segmentation would mainly duplicate the represented construction and its stated consequences, isolate routine displayed algebra whose exact typography is extraction-unsafe, or select bibliography and acknowledgements. The source's substantive epsilon-family reference note was retained, and the unresolved domain/completeness caveat was retained as material negative evidence.
stop_reason: Stopped only after the final source line because the complete normalized article was inspected: the central difference/Hurwitz/boundary mechanism, symmetry and biorthogonal heuristics, degeneracy and regularization consequences, epsilon deformation, and every source-stated mathematical obstruction are represented; the remainder is repeated summary, standard orientation, formula-detail needing scan verification, page furniture, acknowledgements, or bibliography.
